planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; a true wild species native to South Korea.

directions: Native to the Baekun-san mountain area of South Korea, Hemerocallis hakuunensis is a true wild species long gathered locally as a spring vegetable as well as grown ornamentally. It forms a clump of grassy, arching foliage and sends up slender scapes bearing bright orange, trumpet-shaped flowers in summer. Grow it as a species collector's plant in average, well-drained garden soil, dividing crowded clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor and bloom.
sources: Plants of the World Online (Kew Science)

common_name: Double River Wye Daylily (Semi-Double Lemon Yellow Daylily)

planting.note: Plant bare-root fans or container divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: Double River Wye is a tetraploid daylily grown for its semi-double to fully double, light lemon-yellow blooms, with extra, thickened petals washed green at the heart and held on sturdy midseason scapes. The double form is reliably consistent in cool weather and only occasionally reverts to single flowers during the hottest part of summer. It is a dependable, problem-free clump-former suited to mixed borders, and its lush deciduous foliage stays tidy from spring until dormancy.

common_name: Wind Frills Daylily (Pink Crispate-Form Fragrant Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; evergreen-type foliage benefits from a sheltered site in the colder part of its range.

directions: Wind Frills is a diploid, evergreen-foliage daylily grown mainly for its distinctive crispate flower form, in which the pink petals pinch and twist along their length rather than lying flat, giving each large bloom a feminine, windblown look. Flowers carry a yellow-green throat and noticeable fragrance, opening from early into midseason. Because it keeps evergreen foliage, it performs best in milder climates or a protected microclimate where winter dieback is minimal.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average garden soil in full sun; a tough, dormant-foliage heirloom that tolerates a wide range of conditions.

directions: Butterpat is a long-grown diploid heirloom daylily with smooth, rounded, medium-yellow self-colored flowers held on compact, well-proportioned scapes in midseason. Its fragrant blooms open in late afternoon or evening and persist into the next day, a trait sometimes described as nocturnal or extended. Vigorous and dormant-foliage hardy, it is an easy-care clump-former well suited to mixed perennial borders or a historic daylily collection.

planting.note: Non-climbing herbaceous type; stake loosely or let it lean into neighboring plants, and cut stems back hard after flowering or in late winter.

directions: Unlike the purple-leaved 'Purpurea' selection grown chiefly for foliage color, the straight species Clematis recta keeps plain green leaves throughout the season. It is a non-climbing, herbaceous species native to central and southern Europe that sends up upright, bushy stems topped in early summer with large, airy clusters of small, star-shaped, vanilla-scented white flowers, followed by decorative silvery seedheads. Left unsupported it sprawls rather than climbs, so stake it or let it scramble through sturdy border companions, and cut the clump back hard after bloom to keep it tidy.

common_name: Stans Bush Clematis (Non-Vining Japanese Bell-Flowered Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; a non-vining sub-shrub that needs no climbing support.

directions: Clematis stans is a Japanese species in the same non-climbing, sub-shrubby group as the better-known C. heracleifolia and C. tubulosa, forming an upright to sprawling mound of coarse, deeply veined foliage. From late summer into fall it bears clusters of small, tubular, bell-shaped flowers in pale lilac to soft blue with recurved tips. Rather than scaling a support, it works best massed at the front of a sunny border or alongside other herbaceous perennials; cut the woody-based stems back in late winter to refresh growth.

planting.note: Plant in spring against a sheltered wall, fence, or trellis in well-drained soil; roots appreciate cool, shaded conditions even where the vine climbs into sun.

directions: Native to China and Japan, Clematis finetiana is an evergreen climbing species with glossy, leathery leaflets and clusters of small, fragrant, pure white star-shaped flowers in spring, followed by silky seedheads. It climbs by twining leaf stalks onto a wall, fence, or shrub support and holds its foliage through mild winters, making it a good companion for C. armandii or C. cirrhosa where a milder-climate evergreen clematis is wanted. Site it where its roots stay cool and shaded while the top growth reaches toward sun.

planting.note: Plant in spring in a warm, sheltered spot with a sturdy climbing support; best suited to subtropical gardens or a large container that can be protected from frost.

directions: Clematis meyeniana is a vigorous, evergreen climbing species from southern China, Taiwan, and the Philippines, bearing glossy, leathery leaflets and abundant clusters of small, fragrant white flowers in spring. It is considerably more cold-tender than the East Asian evergreen species more commonly grown in temperate gardens, and performs best where winters stay mild. Give it a sturdy fence, arbor, or tree to scramble into, and expect rampant growth in warm, humid climates.
sources: Plants of the World Online (Kew Science)

common_name: Forster's Clematis (New Zealand Native Evergreen Species)

planting.note: Plant in spring in a sheltered, frost-free or near frost-free site; dioecious, so a male and female plant are both needed to set the ornamental seed heads.

directions: Native to New Zealand, Clematis forsteri is a scrambling, evergreen species with small, leathery, divided leaves and clusters of starry, cream to pale yellow-green flowers carrying a light, sweet fragrance, typically in late winter and spring. Like many New Zealand clematis it is dioecious, with separate male and female plants, and distinctly more frost-tender than the familiar European and Asian garden hybrids. Grow it over a low fence or shrub in a mild coastal-style garden, or in a large container that can be moved under cover in cold weather.

planting.note: Plant in spring in a sheltered, frost-free or near frost-free site with a tall support or tree canopy to climb into; dioecious, so both sexes are needed for fruit set.

directions: Known to the Maori as puawananga and regarded as New Zealand's most spectacular native clematis, Clematis paniculata is a vigorous evergreen climber that scrambles high into forest canopy in the wild. In spring it produces a profusion of large, fragrant, pure white flowers that can smother the vine in bloom, followed by fluffy silver seed heads on the female plants. It needs a frost-free or near frost-free climate and a substantial tree, trellis, or arbor to climb, and like other New Zealand clematis it is dioecious, so both a male and female plant are required if seed heads are wanted.
